rate best defines the:

required margin.

feedback.neutral:
B is correct because this specified yield spread over the reference rate is called the 
quoted margin on the FRN. The role of the quoted margin is to compensate the 
investor for the difference in the credit risk of the issuer and that implied by the 
reference rate.

prompt.text:
A commercial paper has the following characteristics: 
Redemption value $5,000,000 
Interest earned $140,500 
Days to maturity 160 
 
For a 365-day year, the discount rate is closest to:

feedback.neutral:
B is correct because the discount rate, DR = (Year/Days) × ((FV – PV)/FV), where 
Year = number of days in the year, Days = number of days between settlement and 
maturity, FV = future value paid at maturity/face value of the money market 
instrument, PV = present value/price of the money market instrument, and FV – PV, 
is the interest earned. 
DR = (365/160) × (140,500/5,000,000) = 0.0641 ≈ 6.4%.

prompt.text:
A floating-rate note makes semiannual interest payments and has a coupon rate 
equal to the six-month market reference rate plus 45 basis points. The interest 
payments are made in June and December. If the six-month market reference rate 
was 1.95% in June and 2.25% in December of the same year, the coupon rate paid in 
December of that year was closest to:

feedback.neutral:
A is correct because the applicable interest rate in December is the six -month 
market reference rate in June plus the 45 basis point margin = 1.95% + 0.45% = 
2.40%.

prompt.text:
If the yield to maturity on an annual -pay bond is 7.75%, the bond-equivalent yield 
yield on semi-annual basis is closest to:

choices:
7.61%. 
 
 
  
Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Floating-Rate Instruments 
Faculty:                                                                                    Page 4 of 7

feedback.neutral:
C is correct. The most common periodicity for US dollar-denominated bond yields is 
two because most bonds in the US dollar market make semiannual coupon payments. 
An annual rate having a periodicity of two is known as a semiannual bond basis yield, or 
semiannual bond equivalent yield. Therefore, a semiannual bond basis yield is the yield 
per semiannual period times two. For this example, we need to take the YTM of the 
annual coupon bond, which is an effective annual rate, and convert it to a semiannual 
bond equivalent yield: 2 × (1.07750.5 – 1) = 0.07605 or 7.61%.
